# Conservative Party Manifesto 2024 Summary

## Economy and Taxation
The manifesto proposes cutting employee National Insurance from 12% to 6% by April 2027, abolishing the main rate of self-employed National Insurance, and introducing "Triple Lock Plus" to ensure the State Pension and pensioner tax allowances rise with the highest of inflation, earnings, or 2.5%. The party commits to not raising income tax, VAT, or Capital Gains Tax, and pledges to extend existing business tax incentives.

## Public Services
NHS spending would increase above inflation annually, with targets to recruit 92,000 additional nurses and 28,000 more doctors. The manifesto includes expanding Pharmacy First, building 250 GP surgeries, and establishing 50 Community Diagnostic Centres. Mental health support would be expanded to all schools by 2030.

## Immigration and Borders
A legally binding annual cap on migration would be introduced, requiring parliamentary approval. The Rwanda removal scheme would continue. Illegal migrants would face removal, and asylum claims would be processed within six months.

## Defence and Security
Defence spending would increase to 2.5% of GDP by 2030, with £10 billion invested in UK munitions production. Support for Ukraine would continue at current levels.

## Housing
The target is 1.6 million new homes in England, with permanent Stamp Duty abolition for first-time buyers on homes up to £425,000. A new Help to Buy scheme would provide 20% equity loans. Leasehold reform would cap ground rents at £250.

## Energy and Environment
Annual oil and gas licensing rounds would continue, alongside trebling offshore wind capacity and building new nuclear plants including Small Modular Reactors. Net zero remains the target for 2050.

## Education and Youth
Mandatory National Service would be introduced for 18-year-olds, offering either competitive military placements or weekend civic service. The manifesto proposes 100,000 new apprenticeships funded by closing underperforming university courses, and statutory bans on mobile phones in schools.

## Transport
The £2 bus fare cap would be extended. £36 billion from HS2 savings would fund regional transport projects, including £8.3 billion for road repairs.

## Devolution
Continued direct funding to Scotland, Wales, and Northern Ireland is pledged, alongside protection of the UK internal market and extension of investment zones and freeports across all nations.
